description: PULP APB3 GPIO F5 behavior with a declared cause bit: INTSTATUS (0x24, ro, read_clears) bit 0 is the pin-0 cause the ISR reads. The pad model and trigger sequence are unchanged.
notes: F5 facts and the pins block come from configs/scenarios/inprocess-obi-apb-gpio-pins.json, which declares trigger_offsets [4, 24, 28, 12], status_offset 36, source_port interrupt, source_bit_offset 0, pulse_width_ticks 16 and pins {padin_offset 8, external_value 0, pad_resolution device_drives_when_dir_bit_high_else_host}

the trigger values are the reviewed sequence recorded in configs/scenarios/inprocess-obi-apb-gpio-pins-f1f5.json: GPIOEN(4)=0xffffffff, INTEN(24)=1, INTTYPE_LOW(28)=1 (pin 0 rise) and PADOUT(12)=43 (0x2b, the pin-0 rise the device's own edge probe observes)

the last PADOUT value is case stimulus in scripts/run_inprocess_gpio.py (its F5 record carries the per-offset values); 43 is the value of the recorded run runs/stage2-breadth-gpio-20261101/run1 (F5:ffffffff:00000001:00000001:0000002b) and of the f1f5 scenario, not a property of the device
pins: PADIN at offset 8 is the readable pad word, external_value 0 is the host driver value, and a pin is driven by the device's own out bit while its dir bit is high

this file states device facts only: the executor still cross-checks them against configs/peripherals/pulp_gpio_causal_local/component_profile.json, and the declaration does not prove the pad causality
status_cause_bits [0] is the profile's INTSTATUS bit 0 and is sampled from the ISR's real read; a declared cause bit is not a device acknowledgement claim.
